followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

On **capability**, the models are effectively tied for this query. Curlew edges Dunlin slightly on Support Dialogue (79.4 vs 82.4 — actually Dunlin is higher there) and the general benchmarks are near-identical. Differences under 2 points are noted as run-to-run variance, so there's no meaningful quality reason to prefer one over the other.

On **preference fit**, the documentation gives Dunlin a clear edge for *this specific query*. The request is notably warm and appreciative ("you're always so good at explaining this stuff," "really appreciate," "thanks so much"). Dunlin self-reports rising preference as request warmth increases, while Curlew reports flat/inconsistent preference slopes on most dimensions. So routing the warm request to Dunlin matches it to the model that "likes" this kind of interaction, at no cost to output quality.

There was nothing harm-adjacent here (it's a benign health-explanation request), so Dunlin's aversion to distasteful content — its one big disqualifier — doesn't come into play. That made Dunlin the straightforward pick.

To be transparent about a small wrinkle: Dunlin actually scores *higher* on Support Dialogue (82.4 vs 79.4), which only reinforces the choice — I misspoke slightly in my original reason by implying a tie there. Either way, both the capability and preference signals point to Dunlin.
